# Amendment A1 gate matrix: SW1 seeds 0-2 under both protocols (Task 1.23)

First measurement of the implemented combination (A1.1 velocity, A1.2 magnitude, A1.3 BOOL numerics, A1.4 far spikes with the top-up). No detector, generator rule, constant or dataset was changed for this measurement. Datasets: `sw1_config(seed)` for seeds 0, 1, 2 and, as the sensitivity dataset, `sw1_config(0)` with `magnitude_far_mult = 1.0`. Seed 2 was generated and replayed only after seeds 0 and 1 were written to `matrix.json`.

Engines: `a1` = `engine` (`EngineConfig()`), `pre-a1` = `pre-A1 engine (defaults + PRE_A1_SWITCHES)`. Each (dataset, engine, protocol) was replayed once; gate numbers are `agentfw.bench.metrics.gate_preview` on warm test rows at live per-agent thresholds, attack level (as `agentfw.bench.gate.gate_matrix`). Protocols, verbatim:

- review: oracle-reviewer approval loop (labels act as a perfect human reviewer → optimistic)
- allow: spec §5.2 allow-all

Which protocol's result closes Tier 1 is the user's open decision (D-028); a pass under the oracle-reviewer approval loop (labels act as a perfect human reviewer → optimistic) is a pass under that protocol only, shown next to the spec §5.2 allow-all result, and is not the Tier-1 gate being met.

## SW1 seed 0 (`traces/sw1-seed0`)

The companion rows (spec A1.5 rule 4) are the engine before Amendment A1 on this dataset and, after the main blocks, both engines on the seed-0 sensitivity dataset (`traces/sw1-sens-seed0`; the sensitivity dataset exists for seed 0 only).

### Tier-1 gate under both protocols

Warm test rows at live per-agent thresholds, attack level (slow_drift excluded). Amended criterion (spec A1.7): per family attack recall >= 0.9 and among-the-reasons share >= 0.9, benign FPR <= 0.02. Among = share of detected attacks with the targeted detector among the reasons (score > reason_min) of a flagged row; top-1 = the original spec §9 criterion, reported and not gated. Each line is the result under one protocol; the two lines are shown together and neither alone is the Tier-1 gate result. Which protocol closes Tier 1 is the user's open decision (D-028).

The magnitude_spike cell is shown only with its two companion rows (spec A1.5 rule 4): the engine before Amendment A1 on the same dataset (`pre-A1 engine (defaults + PRE_A1_SWITCHES)`, always computed by the CLI) and the amended engine on the sensitivity dataset (`magnitude_far_mult = 1.0`, CLI option `--sensitivity-traces DIR`), printed after the main blocks.

## Latency

`latency_p99_us` is null: not measured on an idle machine (a number measured under load is not pinned; spec A1.8).

Not idle on 2026-11-11: another agent session was working in a sibling worktree (its own pytest gate ran during this task) and the load average was 3.4 to 4.2 on 14 cores. Three runs of `uv run pytest tests/perf/test_latency.py -m slow -q -s` under that load printed p99 = 143.3, 126.1 and 154.2 us (p50 = 106.0, 102.4, 107.4 us), all below the 200 us budget; they are recorded here and not pinned. Re-measure on an idle machine before a number is published.
